title: Multiplicative type persists under flat nilpotent deformation
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal with $I^a=0$ for some integer $a\geq1$, and put $R_0=R/I$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme means a group object in schemes over $S$, and homomorphisms preserve multiplication, identity and inverse. Let $G=\operatorname{Spec}C$ be an affine $S$-group scheme with $C$ a finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Put $G_0=G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ [def-pc-base-change]. A group scheme $\Gamma$ over a scheme $U$ is of multiplicative type if there are an fppf covering $\{V_\alpha\to U\}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] and finitely generated abelian groups $N_\alpha$ with $\Gamma\times_UV_\alpha\simeq D_{V_\alpha}(N_\alpha)$ as $V_\alpha$-group schemes; for a scheme $V$, $D_V(N)$ is obtained by gluing the affine groups $D_A(N)=\operatorname{Spec}A[N]$ with Hopf operations of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. If $G_0$ is of multiplicative type, then $G$ is of multiplicative type. More precisely, if a finitely generated abelian group $N$ and an isomorphism $a_0:G_0\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{R_0}(N)$ are given, there is an $S$-group isomorphism $a:G\xrightarrow{\sim}D_R(N)$ whose reduction is $a_0$. No smoothness assumption is imposed and torsion in $N$ may have order noninvertible in $R$.

source.place: Theorem B.3.2(2), proof, printed p.289, the square-zero deformation assertion for a flat affine group reducing to a diagonalizable group, and its fppf-local form. This is the infinitesimal structural prerequisite, not the complete-local Hom bijection. Online source read; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this group-scheme theorem.

proof.text: First treat the marked split case with $I=J$ and $J^2=0$. Write $B=C/JC\simeq R_0[N]$, using the given $a_0$. Flat tensor exactness identifies $JC=J\otimes_{R_0}B$ and, for $q=2,3$, $J(C^{\otimes_Rq})=J\otimes_{R_0}B^{\otimes_{R_0}q}$. Indeed tensor $0\to J\to R\to R_0\to0$ with the flat module $C^{\otimes_Rq}$; this tensor power is flat by successive tensoring with $C$. Write $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_RC$ for the pullback of multiplication; the affine spectrum, the fibre product of affine spectra [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the algebra tensor pushout identify the group diagrams with the coproduct, counit and inverse identities. Every character $\chi_0:G_0\to\mathbf G_{m,R_0}$, equivalently a group-like unit $v_0\in B$, has a unit lift $v\in C$: lift $v_0$ and its inverse, and invert their product $1+z$ by $1-z$, since $z\in JC$ has square zero.

source.place: Theorem B.3.2(2), square-zero reduction, printed p.289; unit lifting and tensor identifications written out; Stacks 00HD, lemma-flat

proof.text: For such a lift put $1+c=\Delta(v)/(v\otimes v)$. Its reduction is $1$, so $c\in J\otimes_{R_0}(B\otimes_{R_0}B)$. Coassociativity, computed in $C^{\otimes_R3}$, gives $c(h,k)+c(hk,l)=c(k,l)+c(h,kl)$: both sides are the first-order term of $v(hkl)/(v(h)v(k)v(l))$, and products of two $J$-terms vanish. Thus $c$ is a regular two-cocycle for $D_{R_0}(N)$ on the coefficient module $J$ with trivial action, i.e. coaction $j\mapsto j\otimes e_0$. Apply [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-regular-two-cocycle] to get $b\in J\otimes_{R_0}B$ with $c(h,k)=b(k)-b(hk)+b(h)$. Regard $b$ as an element of $JC$ by Step 1. Replacing $v$ by $v'=(1+b)v$ changes the defect to $c+b(hk)-b(h)-b(k)=0$. Hence $\Delta(v')=v'\otimes v'$. Applying the counit gives $\epsilon(v')=\epsilon(v')^2$, and this unit is therefore $1$; the inverse diagram gives the character inverse. Thus $v'$ defines a character lifting $\chi_0$.

source.place: Remark B.2.4, printed p.285, and Theorem B.3.2(2), printed p.289: the degree-two obstruction; explicit unit-valued defect calculation for the smooth target G_m

proof.text: The lift of each character is unique. If $v,w\in C^\times$ are two group-like lifts of the same character, then $w/v=1+x$ for $x\in JC=J\otimes_{R_0}R_0[N]$. The group-like equality says $\Delta(x)=x\otimes1+1\otimes x$, since $J^2=0$. Expand the finitely supported element $x=\sum_n j_ne_n$. For $n\ne0$, the coefficient of $(n,n)$ in $J\otimes_{R_0}R_0[N\times N]$ is $j_n$ on the left and zero on the right. Thus all those $j_n$ vanish. At $(0,0)$ the equality reads $j_0=2j_0$, so $j_0=0$ also. Consequently $x=0$ and $w=v$. This argument allows arbitrary torsion in $N$ and arbitrary $R_0$-module $J$.

source.place: Theorem B.3.2(2), printed p.289: rigidity, here expanded coefficientwise for characters without any smoothness or torsion restriction

proof.text: For every $n\in N$, lift the character represented, under $a_0$, by $e_n\in R_0[N]$ to the unique group-like unit $v_n\in C$. Uniqueness gives $v_{n+n'}=v_nv_{n'}$ and $v_0=1$: both sides lift the same character. Therefore the finite-sum formula $\phi:R[N]\to C$, $\sum_n r_ne_n\mapsto\sum_n r_nv_n$, is an $R$-algebra map. It preserves coproduct and counit on every basis element and carries $e_{-n}$ to $v_n^{-1}$, so it preserves inverse too. Its spectrum is a group homomorphism $a:G\to D_R(N)$ with reduction exactly $a_0$, by affine contravariance.

source.place: Theorem B.3.2(2), printed p.289: reconstruct the diagonalizable-group map from the uniquely lifted characters

proof.text: The map $\phi$ is an isomorphism. Its cokernel $Q$ satisfies $Q/JQ=0$ by tensor right exactness and the isomorphism $\phi\bmod J$. Thus $Q=JQ=J^2Q=0$, so $\phi$ is surjective. Put $K=\ker\phi$. The exact sequence $0\to K\to R[N]\to C\to0$ has flat last term $C$. Tensoring with $R_0$ is therefore still injective on $K/JK$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective]; since $\phi\bmod J$ is an isomorphism, $K/JK=0$. Hence $K=JK=J^2K=0$. This proves the marked assertion for a square-zero ideal.

source.place: Theorem B.3.2(2), printed p.289: isomorphism of flat deformations; explicit cokernel/kernel argument using Stacks 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact, and 00HL, lemma-flat-tor-zero

proof.text: For $I^a=0$ start with $R/I$ and the marking $a_0$. For $1\leq k<a$, pass from $R/I^k$ to $R/I^{k+1}$; the kernel $J_k=I^k/I^{k+1}$ has square zero, since $2k\geq k+1$. The coordinate algebra $C/I^{k+1}C$ is flat over $R/I^{k+1}$: for an injection of quotient-ring modules, tensoring with it is the same as tensoring the original injection over $R$ with $C$, hence preserves injection. Its finite presentation is the original polynomial presentation reduced modulo $I^{k+1}$. Steps 1–5 lift the isomorphism at level $k$ to level $k+1$ with exactly the chosen reduction. After $a-1$ steps obtain the required marked isomorphism over $R/I^a=R$. If $a=1$ the marking itself is the answer. The zero ring is included, since every coordinate algebra and every displayed coefficient then vanishes.

source.place: Theorem B.3.2(2), printed p.289: induction on square-zero thickenings, with the induction variable and base case explicit

proof.text: Now suppose only that $G_0$ is of multiplicative type. Apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-etale-splitting] to choose an affine etale covering $V_j\to\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ and group isomorphisms $(G_0)_{V_j}\simeq D_{V_j}(N_j)$. Lift each $V_j$ to an affine etale $U_j\to S$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-closed-immersion-lift]. The $U_j$ cover $S$: every prime of $R$ contains $I$, every prime of the coordinate ring of $U_j$ contains the extended nilpotent ideal, and the reduced family $V_j$ covers $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$. An etale morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation, so this is an fppf covering.

source.place: Proposition B.3.4, printed pp.291–292; Stacks 09ZA, proof, first paragraph (affine etale lifting), and 021L (definition of fppf covering)

proof.text: Write $U_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$. The group $G_{U_j}$ has flat finitely presented coordinate algebra $A_j\otimes_RC$: the finite presentation is obtained by applying $R\to A_j$ to the finitely many defining polynomials, and flatness follows because tensoring an injection of $A_j$-modules with $A_j\otimes_RC$ is tensoring that injection over $R$ with $C$. Its reduction modulo $IA_j$ is $(G_0)_{V_j}\simeq D_{A_j/IA_j}(N_j)$, and $(IA_j)^a=0$. Apply the marked assertion proved in Step 6 over $A_j$ to get $G_{U_j}\simeq D_{A_j}(N_j)$. These isomorphisms on the fppf cover of Step 7 are exactly the definition of multiplicative type. No gluing of the chosen isomorphisms is required.

The item statement is unchanged and true; this is the first split of a previously empty proof, not a re-split. Steps 1–8 check out. Step 1: J(C^{⊗q}) = J⊗_{R0}B^{⊗q} by flatness of C, and the unit lift is valid. Step 2: the coassociativity defect is exactly the hypothesis of lem-sfb-diagonalizable-regular-two-cocycle with the trivial coaction j↦j⊗e_0; I checked the coboundary sign, and the counit argument holds. Step 3: the coefficientwise comparison at (n,n) and (0,0) needs no division, so p-torsion and characteristic 2 are covered. Step 4: φ is a Hopf map reducing to a_0^*. Step 5: the cokernel is killed by right exactness and the kernel by flat-quotient tensor injectivity with N=R0, both exactly as stated in the cited nodes. Step 6: induction over I^k/I^{k+1}, which has square zero, with the base case a=1. Step 7: the étale lift along Spec R0→Spec R gives a cover because primes contain the nilpotent ideal, and étale implies fppf. Step 8: (IA_j)^a=0, and A_j⊗C is flat and finitely presented. New node lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-etale-splitting: true (Conrad B.3.4; tested on the empty base, μ_p over F_p and μ_n over Q), self-contained, statement-only, with five searches.
